title: Systematic Bug Bounty Methodology — 100 Areas
coreRule: A finding is not a finding until you can write the attacker's exact copy-paste request (Q1). If you can't, KILL it.

lanes.SRC: white-box source review (read code, no live attack)
lanes.LIVE: live testing on an authorized target (human-operated)

priorities.P3: low or hygiene (context, rarely a standalone finding)

items.title: Enumerate all in-scope repos/packages; prefer freshest / recently-changed over hardened flagships; diff the last 60 days.
items.q1: Name the exact repo/commit range you diffed and the changed file that seeds the bug.

items.title: Grep git history for removed secrets/keys/tokens (git log -p, entropy scan) — deleted commits still leak.
items.q1: The exact commit + path + secret value, and the live request that authenticates with it.

items.title: Read every published package (npm/PyPI/Go) in scope, including shipped dist/ and sourcemaps, for endpoints and client secrets.
items.q1: The package version + file + extracted endpoint/secret and the request that uses it.

items.title: Pull JS bundles from in-scope web apps; extract API routes, feature flags, hidden/admin endpoints, client-side secrets.
items.q1: The bundle URL + extracted route/secret and the authenticated request that reaches it.

items.title: Enumerate forgotten/staging subdomains that expose prod data (only if in scope).
items.q1: The in-scope host + the prod data it exposes with a copy-paste request.

items.title: Read OpenAPI / GraphQL schema / .proto / route files — the full endpoint inventory, including legacy and deprecated.
items.q1: The schema file + the specific undocumented/legacy endpoint and its request.

items.title: JWT: alg confusion (none, HS↔RS), missing signature/expiry/audience checks, kid injection.
items.q1: The exact forged/tampered JWT and the request the server accepts it on.

items.title: Password reset: token entropy/expiry, token not bound to the user, host-header poisoning of the reset link, token reuse.
items.q1: The exact reset request (incl. poisoned Host header) and the follow-up that takes over the account.

items.title: Email/phone change without re-auth or without confirmation to the old address → account takeover.
items.q1: The exact change request that mutates the identity without re-auth/confirmation.

items.title: OAuth: redirect_uri validation, state/PKCE presence, code/token leakage via referer or open redirect, account-link to attacker-controlled identity.
items.q1: The exact authorize request with attacker redirect_uri and where the code/token lands.

items.title: Magic-link / session-transfer: is the id a signed/expiring token or a guessable value?
items.q1: The guessable id and the request that rides it into another user's session.

items.title: MFA bypass: skip-step, brute-forceable OTP, remember-device forgery, weak backup codes.
items.q1: The exact request that reaches the authenticated state without a valid second factor.

items.title: Session: fixation, insufficient invalidation on logout / password change, predictable tokens.
items.q1: The session id that stays valid after logout/reset, shown by a post-invalidation request.

items.title: Auth check that renders/continues after failure (missing return after a 401/403).
items.q1: The request that fails the check yet still receives the protected response body.

items.title: IDOR / BOLA: object fetched by user-supplied id without scoping to the caller (Model.find(params[:id]) unscoped).
items.q1: The exact request swapping an id that returns another user's object.

items.title: CWE-639: authoritative identity read from a request field/body, never bound to the authenticated channel.
items.q1: The request whose body/param identity overrides the session identity.

items.title: Read-path vs write-path parity: does update/delete re-check what the read path checked?
items.q1: The write/delete request that succeeds where the read path would have denied it.

items.title: Function-level authz: privileged/admin action missing its role gate.
items.q1: The exact privileged request that a normal (or no) role can call.

items.title: Horizontal (peer objects across accounts) and vertical (admin functions as a normal user) escalation.
items.q1: The exact request that crosses the account/role boundary.

items.title: Mass assignment: permit includes role/owner/is_admin/account_id — can you set a privileged attribute?
items.q1: The exact body that sets a privileged attribute and the state it changes.

items.title: Elevated-authority (service/system) call that skips the caller's per-object permission (confused deputy).
items.q1: The request that makes the privileged component act on an object the caller cannot access.

items.title: Check on the object in the URL vs the object in the body — mismatched authorization.
items.q1: The request whose URL object is authorized but body object is not.

items.title: Cross-tenant read: tenant/org id from the request used as the trust anchor instead of the session's tenant.
items.q1: The request with a swapped tenant/org id that returns another tenant's data.

items.title: Non-injective cache/session keys → one tenant served another tenant's cached data or identity.
items.q1: The two inputs that collide to one cache key and the leaked cross-tenant response.

items.title: Cross-tenant write: create/modify objects in another tenant by swapping ids.
items.q1: The write request that mutates another tenant's object.

items.title: A code path missing the tenant filter / row-level-security scope.
items.q1: The query/handler missing the tenant scope and the request that reaches it.

items.title: Enumerable tenant identifiers (sequential ids, predictable slugs) enabling systematic cross-tenant access.
items.q1: The id/slug pattern and a request that walks it into another tenant.

items.title: Price/quantity/currency tampering; negative quantities; integer over/underflow on totals.
items.q1: The exact order/checkout request with the tampered value and the resulting total.

items.title: Race conditions: double-spend, coupon/credit re-use, concurrent withdrawal (TOCTOU).
items.q1: The two+ concurrent requests and the invariant they break.

items.title: State-machine abuse: skip required steps, replay a step, reach a terminal state early.
items.q1: The out-of-order request sequence that reaches the illegal state.

items.title: Coupon/referral/credit abuse: stacking, self-referral, unlimited application.
items.q1: The request sequence that applies the credit beyond its intended limit.

items.title: Server trusts client-supplied prices/totals/flags instead of recomputing server-side.
items.q1: The request whose client-supplied price/flag the server persists without recompute.

items.title: Quota/limit bypass via account recreation or parallel requests beating the check.
items.q1: The requests that exceed the quota and the enforced limit they beat.

items.title: Excessive data exposure: endpoint returns more fields than the UI shows — read the serializer for secrets/PII/internal flags.
items.q1: The endpoint + serializer field (secret/PII) and the request that returns it.

items.title: GraphQL: introspection on, missing field-level authz, alias/batching abuse, nested-query DoS.
items.q1: The exact GraphQL document that leaks a field or amplifies cost.

items.title: Legacy/versioned endpoints (/v1) with weaker checks than current.
items.q1: The legacy endpoint request that bypasses the current check.

items.title: Missing rate limits on sensitive actions (OTP, reset, invite) with demonstrable impact.
items.q1: The unthrottled endpoint and the impact of N requests.

items.title: Output not scope-filtered in a tool/MCP/webhook context (credential-bearing field reaches a log/transcript — CWE-532).
items.q1: The tool/webhook output field carrying a credential and where it lands.

items.title: HTTP method / verb tampering bypassing method-specific auth.
items.q1: The alternate-verb request that bypasses the auth on the intended verb.

items.title: User-supplied URL reaching a server fetch: webhook/callback, avatar/image fetch, URL importer, PDF/HTML renderer.
items.q1: The request whose URL parameter makes the server fetch an attacker-chosen target.

items.title: Allowlist bypass: parser differentials, DNS rebinding, redirect-following, decimal/octal IP, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254).
items.q1: The exact URL that passes the allowlist yet resolves to the internal/metadata target.

items.title: Blind SSRF via out-of-band interaction (log the seed; hand chaining to the human).
items.q1: The request + OOB collaborator URL and the observed callback.

items.title: Second-order SSRF: a stored URL fetched later by a backend job.
items.q1: The write that stores the URL and the later job that fetches it.

items.title: SQL/NoSQL: string-concatenated queries, unparameterized raw ORM calls (report the sink).
items.q1: The sink line and the request payload that alters the query.

items.title: Command injection: user input reaching exec/system/shell.
items.q1: The request payload that executes an attacker command.

items.title: SSTI: user input into a template engine (Jinja/ERB/Handlebars).
items.q1: The template payload and its evaluated output.

items.title: LDAP / XPath / header injection; CRLF in redirects and headers.
items.q1: The payload and the injected query/header/redirect it produces.

items.title: XXE: XML parser with external entities enabled on a user-supplied document.
items.q1: The exact XML document and the file/SSRF it reads back.

items.title: Stored/reflected/DOM XSS; markdown/HTML sanitizer bypass; SVG/attachment XSS.
items.q1: The exact payload and the context it executes in.

items.title: postMessage: missing/permissive event.origin check; a second listener that forgot the check the main one has.
items.q1: The attacker-origin postMessage payload and the privileged action it triggers.

items.title: CORS: reflected Origin with credentials; wildcard with allow-credentials.
items.q1: The cross-origin request with credentials and the response ACAO/ACAC headers.

items.title: CSRF on state-changing endpoints lacking token/SameSite, with real impact.
items.q1: The auto-submitting cross-site request and the state it changes.

items.title: Clickjacking on auth-state-changing pages (context; low value alone).
items.q1: The framing PoC page and the action it tricks a click into.

items.title: Prototype pollution (client or server JS) leading to authz/logic bypass or RCE.
items.q1: The payload polluting __proto__ and the gadget it flips.

items.title: Unrestricted upload → RCE (webshell); content-type/extension bypass; SVG/HTML stored XSS.
items.q1: The exact upload request and the URL that executes/serves it.

items.title: Path traversal in upload/download/read (../, encoded, absolute) → arbitrary file read/write.
items.q1: The exact path parameter and the file it reads/writes outside the root.

items.title: Insecure deserialization: pickle/marshal/yaml.load/Java/PHP unserialize on user data.
items.q1: The serialized payload and the code it executes on load.

items.title: Zip-slip / archive-extraction traversal; symlink following.
items.q1: The crafted archive entry path and the file it writes outside the target dir.

items.title: Presigned-URL / storage misuse: overbroad scope, predictable keys, cross-tenant object paths.
items.q1: The presigned request/object key that reaches another tenant's object.

items.title: Hardcoded credentials/keys/tokens in source, config, JS bundles, mobile binaries.
items.q1: The file + secret value and the live request that authenticates with it.

items.title: Secrets recoverable from git history.
items.q1: The commit + path + secret and the request that uses it.

items.title: Verbose errors / stack traces leaking internals, paths, tokens.
items.q1: The request that triggers the leak and the sensitive line returned.

items.title: PII/secret over-exposure in API responses, logs, or LLM/tool outputs; redaction applied inconsistently across endpoints.
items.q1: The endpoint/log line + the sensitive field and the request that returns it.

items.title: Exposed .env/.git/backup files, debug endpoints, actuator/metrics, prod sourcemaps.
items.q1: The exact URL that returns the exposed file/endpoint.

items.title: Sensitive data in URLs/query strings (tokens in referer-leaking links).
items.q1: The URL carrying the token and the referer sink that leaks it.

items.title: Signature verification bypass: missing check, wrong message/domain, ecrecover malleability, ERC-1271 misuse.
items.q1: The message + signature the verifier wrongly accepts.

items.title: Replay: missing nonce/timestamp/expiry; domain-separator reuse across chains/contexts.
items.q1: The captured request replayed successfully a second time/context.

items.title: Non-constant-time comparison of secrets/HMACs/signatures.
items.q1: The compare sink and the timing oracle it exposes.

items.title: Weak randomness for tokens/keys/nonces (Math.random, predictable seeds).
items.q1: The generator sink and the predicted value used in a request.

items.title: Webhook signature not verified, verified against an attacker-controllable secret, or timing-unsafe.
items.q1: The forged webhook request the handler accepts.

items.title: Map the ONE trust boundary per component: where identity/origin/trust is decided (cert vs token vs cookie vs param).
items.q1: The component + the exact line where trust is decided, and what crosses it unchecked.

items.title: Grep the identity flow: cert/subject/JWT-claim absence next to an identity taken from the request.
items.q1: The line reading identity from the request where the channel identity should win.

items.title: Parser/normalization differentials: two components parse the same input differently (path, unicode, content-type).
items.q1: The single input and the two divergent parses that create the bypass.

items.title: Missing return after an early auth failure.
items.q1: The handler line where execution falls through after a 401/403.

items.title: TOCTOU between check and use, visible in source.
items.q1: The check line and the use line with the window between them.

items.title: Diff the latest release/PRs for newly introduced auth/identity/payment code — bugs cluster in new code.
items.q1: The PR/commit and the new auth/payment line that carries the flaw.

items.title: MCP/tool authz: a read-only (SELECT-only) query interface that can be escaped to writes.
items.q1: The exact tool call payload that performs a write through the read-only interface.

items.title: MCP tool output not scope-filtered → secrets into model context/logs.
items.q1: The tool output field carrying a secret and where it lands in context/logs.

items.title: Direct prompt injection in LLM-powered endpoints altering privileged behavior.
items.q1: The exact prompt and the privileged action it induces.

items.title: Indirect prompt injection via ingested data (annotations, docs, RAG sources).
items.q1: The poisoned document and the resulting privileged action.

items.title: Training-data / model / system-prompt exfiltration via API.
items.q1: The request that returns the system prompt/training data.

items.title: Agent/tool constructing requests with unscoped identity or an over-broad API key.
items.q1: The code building the downstream request with the wrong/over-broad identity.

items.title: Hardcoded secrets/keys/endpoints in APK/IPA/desktop binary.
items.q1: The binary + extracted secret and the request that uses it.

items.title: Insecure local storage of tokens/PII (plaintext prefs, unprotected keychain/DB).
items.q1: The storage location and the plaintext sensitive value in it.

items.title: Improper TLS/cert validation, pinning bypass, cleartext traffic allowed.
items.q1: The setting/code disabling validation and the MITM it permits.

items.title: Exported/unprotected components (activities/services/receivers/providers); deeplink/intent handling.
items.q1: The exported component and the intent/deeplink that abuses it.

items.title: Insecure update / missing code-signing verification.
items.q1: The update path that accepts an unsigned/attacker artifact.

items.title: WebView misconfig (JS bridge exposure, file access).
items.q1: The WebView setting and the bridge call it exposes.

items.title: Subdomain takeover (dangling CNAME to an unclaimed service).
items.q1: The dangling host + CNAME target and the claim that proves control.

items.title: Open S3/GCS buckets with sensitive data (real impact only).
items.q1: The bucket URL and the sensitive object it lists/returns.

items.title: Exposed admin dashboards/panels without auth.
items.q1: The URL that reaches the admin panel without auth.

items.title: Missing security headers / CSP — context, not a finding without an exploit chain.
items.q1: The missing header AND the concrete exploit it enables (else KILL).

items.title: SPF/DKIM/DMARC gaps — low value unless they enable real phishing/impact.
items.q1: The spoofed email that lands AND the impact (else KILL).

items.title: Overly-permissive cloud IAM / service roles, if reachable and demonstrable.
items.q1: The reachable role and the privileged action it performs.

items.title: 7-Question Gate before any report. Q1: write the exact copy-paste attacker request or KILL it.
items.q1: This IS Q1. No request, no report.

items.title: Seed-and-stop: a source-evident seed hands live escalation/chaining to the human.
items.q1: State the seed and the exact live step handed to the operator.

items.title: Scope is law: re-check every asset against the in-scope line; out-of-scope is not a finding.
items.q1: Cite the in-scope line that authorizes this exact asset.

items.title: Honest severity, own words, permalink pinned to the commit. A clean Low builds the record.
items.q1: State severity in your own words with a commit-pinned permalink.

items.title: Dedup: if it's easy to find on a crowded flagship, assume it's already reported.
items.q1: State why this is not already reported (freshness/obscurity).

items.title: Honest base rate: most reviews find nothing. Log the empty, move to the next fresh target.
items.q1: If nothing survives Q1, log the empty result honestly and move on.
